pr_title: Look up todoist collaborators only when adding new task
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This makes an improvement to looking up collaborators. There isn't a single endpoint to fetch all collaborators.  The only way to retrieve them is to [request them by project id](https://developer.todoist.com/rest/v2/?shell#get-all-collaborators).  What we were originally doing is looking them all up when setting up the integration.  If you have a lot of projects that means we were sending off multiple requests at once (1 per project).  This would cause a warning to be emitted in the logs: `Connection pool is full, discarding connection: api.todoist.com. Connection pool size: 10`

Collaborators are only used when adding a task using the `todoist.add_task`  service.  Since we have the project_id when adding the task, I've moved looking up the collaborators into the service call which results in only a single api call and only if the user specified an assignee.

I also fixed 2 bugs that I noticed when looking at the [api docs for this endpoint](https://developer.todoist.com/rest/v2/?shell#create-a-new-task):
* `assignee` param should have been `assignee_id`.
* The `label_ids` param should have been `labels` and it should be a list of strings, not ids.

**NOTE**: This PR alone doesn't completely fix the issue, there is a 2nd task that I"ll do in a separate PR to handle [that](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/87335#issuecomment-1426847663).

Same here. Is this problem rooted in the Todoist integration for home assistant or directly at Todoist (API)? Maybe @boralyl can help?

Looked into this briefly.  Before the integration broke it was using the sync-api.  Essentially it made a single request and retrieved all project and task data.

The rest-api works differently and data must be requested separately in some instances.  I do see some areas for improvement to reduce the connections and get rid of the warnings:

1. There isn't an api endpoint to fetch all collaborators. So when the component is setup it issues a request to get collaborators for every project. So if you had 10 projects we'd fire off 10 requests right off the bat.  This appears to only be used so that you can specify an assignee when using the create task service. I'm not sure if anyone uses this feature or not.  I believe this could be fixed by simply fetching collaborators at the time of calling the create new task service.
2. When fetching events for the calendar or updating one of the calendar entities we issue 1 request per project.  This could be improved to use a [DataUpdateCoordinator](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/integration_fetching_data/#coordinated-single-api-poll-for-data-for-all-entities) to make a single request to get all tasks rather than 1 request per project.

I believe addressing those 2 tasks should resolve the warnings in the logs.  Both of these would be separate tasks to keep PR's focused so I wouldn't expect fixing only 1 of the above to resolve the warnings.

Still getting this error on HA 2023.3.0.

@boralyl - any thoughts on if/when this can be fixed? Thanks :)
